fact: Ecofin Agency reports Mauritania launched its national cloud on 29 June 2026 at the National Data Center in Nouakchott to host government data and digital public services domestically.
Ecofin Agency reports the government launched a national cloud to gradually centralise government digital services, with no migration timeline announced.
Elilam reports the national government cloud now hosts state services under full sovereignty, as stated at the digital ministry training opening.

Al Wiam reports AN-ETAT briefed the World Bank vice president on the WARDIP-funded national government cloud project, including data-security testing and preparations to migrate government systems and data ahead of go-live.
Agence Ecofin reports Mauritania launched its national cloud on 29 June 2026 at the Nouakchott National Data Centre to host public administration data and digital services on national territory.
Agence Ecofin reports the ministry did not give a migration timetable for administrations' applications and databases to the new national cloud.

The ministry (MTNMA), through WARDIP, launched a tender on 17 September 2024 for a government cloud, and describes the national Tier III data centre as enabling national hosting of government data and applications.
Minister of Digital Transformation told the National Assembly that all government servers were moved into a data centre the ministry built to international standards.
Minister said Mauritania launched its first national cloud days earlier, ending reliance on foreign clouds for digital services.
The ministry's representative says works have begun on a national cloud system.
The national Nouakchott Data Center is stated to store and protect sovereign data and to offer cloud hosting within national borders to public and private institutions.
The ministry's communique says the national government cloud is meant to host State services while respecting digital sovereignty, among applications already engaged under the Digital-Y project.
